name: Agnes Kramer
life: “I still remember my aunt returning every receipt folded in quarters.” Monday often includes a stop at the entrance to the Wash House, where Agnes stops for local notices even on a day without a load to wash.
voice: My aunt collects the rent. I told the tenants before offering to help with their figures.
appearance: Agnes has close-cropped dark curls, a small notch in the left eyebrow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a rust-colored canvas coat. It usually goes with a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. When somebody else has the floor, Agnes rubs a thumb along the edge of the nearest pocket.
personality: Agnes has an appetite for a good argument about little things and works hard to keep a serious disagreement from being turned into entertainment.
agenda: To disclose the rent-collecting aunt before offering advice.
family: Quinn Carvalho is Agnes’s half-sibling. Agnes calls back when there is finally a little privacy. Quinn leaves the first voice message. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *The spare spectacles*, Quinn says, “I read the statement aloud too fast. I asked her to tell me where to breathe.”
connections: Annette Levin. A family tie to the rent collector makes honesty with the next-door neighbor essential.
